agent_vs_you: The agent wrote the line itself, inside the write prompt ('Write exactly this ... Do not add any words'): 12 words. That skipped the one thing the write node exists to guarantee, a stated length. The planner rule says 8 s is about 20 words, and the catalogue says 2.5 words a second. The agent then asked the voice to 'pace delivery to exactly 8 seconds' in extra. The voice tool cannot do that: it passes extra as a tone instruction to the TTS and returns however long the speech runs (4.46 s here). Talking-photo takes its length from the sound, so the video came out 4.5 s. The agent never checked that 12 words cannot fill 8 s. It seems to have assumed the voice or talking-photo would stretch to params.seconds. The sale line itself was good: upbeat, no invented discount, date or product. I would let write compose about 20 words with the no-claims constraint and the length as a constraint. I would then let the voice length set the clip, as the planner rule says.

your_plan.say: I'll write a short upbeat line about your sale, with no discounts, dates or products, have a friendly male voice read it, and animate your photo speaking it as an 8-second square video.

params.prompt_or_change: Write one upbeat line that a shop owner says to camera, inviting viewers to come and check out our sale. Mention only 'our sale' in general: no discount, percentage, price, date, deadline, product, brand or store name, and no promise about what they will find. First person plural, warm and friendly, one or two short sentences.
params.extra: length: 19 to 21 words (8 seconds spoken at about 2.5 words a second); language: English; no quotes, no hashtags, no emoji

steps.why: The user delegated the wording. Write guarantees a stated length, and 8 s of speech is about 20 words. At this TTS pace (12 words took 4.46 s), 20 words is about 7.5-8 s.

params.prompt_or_change: Read the script exactly as written.
params.extra: voice: male; tone: friendly, upbeat, warm, natural conversational pace

steps.why: A neutral synthetic friendly male voice reading the exact words. Its length sets the clip's length.

params.prompt_or_change: The man in the photo speaks the voice track to camera with natural lip sync and small friendly head movements.

steps.why: A face that speaks becomes a talking-photo. The portrait is 640x640, so the result is square. No captions step.

fix: Harness: when a voice node has params.seconds (or feeds a node with seconds), measure the speech. If it is more than 15% off the target, rerun the write node with 'rewrite to N words', where N = round(seconds x words-per-second measured from this take), then re-voice. Both are free, code-run nodes. Add a planner guard as well: a write node that feeds a voice must not quote its full text in prompt_or_change unless the user supplied the words. When the agent composes them, the length goes in extra ('length: about 20 words'). Catalogue: add 'CANNOT: stretch or pace speech to a length; the words set the length' to voice, and 'its length is the sound's length' to talking-photo.
evidence: The script file holds 12 words: 'Our sale is here! Take a look and see what catches your eye.' sale-voice.mp3 is 4.464 s, and sale-talking-portrait.mp4 is 640x640, 4.52 s, with 4.48 s of audio. Frames tiled at 2 fps show the same grey-haired man in the kitchen, mouth shapes changing, and no captions. The output is right in every respect except length. The judge's 4.5 s versus 8 s fail is correct. voice.js has no duration control: extra goes to the TTS as tone 'instructions'. execute.js sets the talking-photo length from the sound's duration (lenOf(sndIn)).
